statuses.title: Compare optimizer drift fingerprints in float64
statuses.note: Fix commit 6ea47e6e. All five previously-untyped float comparisons are converted: the four fingerprint statistics (packages/opaque-optimizers/src/opaque/api/optimizers/distributed.py:119-122) and the plain-float leaf at :148 now route through the new _assert_float_equal (:73-86), which passes compute_dtype=torch.float64 AND atol=0.0/rtol=0.0. That closes both halves OPQ-344 named (the float32 marshalling and, per the finding's own correction, the binding rtol default). I re-read assert_scalar_equal (packages/opaque-engine/src/opaque/api/engine/distributed/_state.py:40-76) to confirm compute_dtype reaches both reduce_scalar calls and the torch.isclose dtype, and ran the two gloo tests (`pytest packages/opaque-optimizers/tests/ddp/ -m distributed` -> 2 passed), including the new test_optimizer_state_audit_detects_micro_scale_drift which exercises the 1e-6 relative drift the old code missed. Caveat (filed as a finding): atol=0/rtol=0 makes the audit fail-closed on reduction-order artifacts. I reproduced a cross-rank FALSE POSITIVE on 2 gloo ranks holding bit-identical AdamState that differ only in torch.get_num_threads() (4 vs 1): OperationError "AdamState.mu['w'].sumsq mismatch across ranks: min=4997394.779571936, max=4997394.7795719365". The old rtol=1e-5 absorbed this. Also note the audit has no production caller - the trainer calls sync() only on clip_state/aux (packages/opaque-transformers/src/opaque/api/transformers/trainer/_dp_trainer.py:2231), never on ctx.opt_state - so both the defect and the fix only reach users who call sync_optimizer_state explicitly.

statuses.title: Correct the Adafactor module docstring's bias-correction and memory claims
statuses.note: Fix commit 7bfba532. All three statements OPQ-345 listed now match the code in the current tree. (1) _adafactor.py:31-32 says 'it defaults to ``False``', matching the signature at :310 `noise_bias_correction: bool = False` and the argument docstring at :339. (2) :28-31 now says the subtraction 'recovers the clean second-moment estimate wherever the result stays positive and falls back to the uncorrected factor elsewhere', matching :245-246 `torch.where(corr_row > 0, corr_row, new_v_row)` / `torch.where(corr_col > 0, corr_col, new_v_col)` and :262 for the unfactored leaf - the 'positive floor' wording is gone. (3) :5-7 now says rank<2 tensors 'keep a full per-element second moment ``v``', matching _init_v_for_leaf's `return (torch.zeros_like(leaf),)` at :123. Sibling check: no other optimizer module claims noise_bias_correction defaults to True; every factory signature in the package is `= False` (_adam.py:282,309; _adadelta.py:326; _adagrad.py:191; _rmsprop.py:203; _radam.py:306; _ademamix.py:226).

statuses.title: Make adadelta mode-switch test perform its promised comparison
statuses.note: Fix commit 8a370bec. Verified by MUTATION, as required. The rewritten test (packages/opaque-optimizers/tests/test_adadelta.py:313-361) now builds a phi-zeroed clone of the same AdadeltaState via dataclasses.replace + tree_map(torch.zeros_like, phi_dx), runs opt.update on both, and asserts torch.equal(updates_live[k], updates_zeroed[k]) at :355, plus phi freeze at :358-361. Three mutation runs against an overlaid copy of the package (PYTHONPATH shadowing, repo untouched): (a) removing BOTH `and noisy_squared_grads is None` conditions -> test FAILS at :355 with tensors differing in the 4th digit, 231 other tests pass; (b) removing ONLY the phi_g guard at _adadelta.py:242 -> FAILS at :355; (c) removing ONLY the two phi_dx guards at :257/:277 -> FAILS at :355. Under the old assertion (torch.isfinite only) all three mutants passed, which is exactly what OPQ-346 reported. Baseline: 232 passed.

statuses.title: Remove unused Adadelta bc_floor plumbing
statuses.note: Fix commit 51fcf562. The dead-code removal itself is complete and correct: `grep -rn bc_floor packages/ docs/` now returns zero hits in _adadelta.py; the parameter is gone from _scale_by_adadelta's signature and `bc_floor = eps * eps` is gone from adadelta(). Every surviving bc_floor is live (_rmsprop.py:128, _adam.py:197, _radam.py:240, _ademamix.py:139). The commit also fixed a fourth doc-drift OPQ-347 did not list: the module docstring's `E[dx^2]_corrected = max(E[dx^2] - phi_dx, eps^2)` became the accurate where-fallback at _adadelta.py:26-27. No state-dict/back-compat impact: bc_floor was a closure argument, never a state field, so serialization round-trips are unaffected (232 optimizer tests pass). Caveat (filed as a finding): OPQ-347's fix sketch offered 'delete the parameter ... or actually apply it in the substitution branch and say which'. Deletion was chosen without saying which, and the substitution branch the finding inspected (_adadelta.py:252-253, `torch.clamp(v_g_corrected, min=0.0)`) turns out not to be benign - it lacks the negative-v fallback that adam/rmsprop/ademamix all apply, and adadelta diverges geometrically on a privatised g-squared stream. OPQ-347's 'No runtime behaviour change' conclusion holds for the removal but its premise that the clamp-plus-eps combination is an adequate guard does not.

findings.title: Adadelta's private second-moment branch diverges geometrically: it lacks the negative-v fallback every sibling optimizer applies
findings.claim: In the `noisy_squared_grads` (private second-moment) branch, `_scale_by_adadelta` guards a possibly-negative second moment with only `v_g_corrected = torch.clamp(v_g_corrected, min=0.0)` (:253). Adam (:197 `torch.where(v_hat > 0, v_hat, m_hat * m_hat).clamp(min=bc_floor)`), RMSprop (:128 `torch.where(v > 0, v, g * g).clamp(min=bc_floor)`) and AdEMAMix (:138) all instead fall back to the squared signal, which is precisely what _adam.py:194-196 documents: 'Falling back to the squared first moment keeps the update magnitude approx 1 ... instead of collapsing the denominator to bc_floor -> infinity update.' In Adadelta the collapse is worse than a one-off spike because it feeds back: clamping to 0 makes `rms_g = sqrt(0 + eps) = 1e-3` (:115-117, :267), so `coef = rms_dx_prev / rms_g` is inflated ~1e3x, `dx = coef * g` is inflated, and `v_dx_new = rho*v_dx + (1-rho)*dx*dx` (:273) carries the inflation into the next step's `rms_dx_prev`. The loop multiplies the update by roughly 4-50x per step.
findings.failure_scenario: A user follows docs/reference/optimizers.md:110-140 ('mf_gaussian_noise(..., second_moment_strategy=...) returns a paired output that Opaque optimizers route automatically') and picks adadelta - the LR-free optimizer the same docs recommend 'when learning-rate tuning is hard' (optimizers.md:48). _chain.py:138 sees `noisy_squared_grads` in the scaler signature and routes the privatised stream in (:172-181). In any realistic high-dimensional DP setting the per-coordinate second-moment signal (~||g||^2/d) is far below the per-coordinate release noise, so ~50% of the stream is negative. Reproduced at d=100000 with unit-norm clipped gradients and per-coordinate noise 1/sqrt(d) (49.99% of the squared stream negative): adadelta max|update| goes 2.0e-2, 8.5e-2, 3.5e-1, 1.2e0, 4.7e0, 1.9e1 ... 9.96e8 at step 19, while adamw/rmsprop/ademamix stay at 8-80 throughout. The repo's own guard test uses the identical fixture and a `< 10.0` bound but runs ONE step: re-running tests/test_adadelta.py:296-307 verbatim for 8 steps instead of 1 gives 1.51e-1, 7.20e0, 3.44e2, 1.64e4, 7.83e5, 3.74e7, 1.78e9, 8.52e10 - it breaches its own assertion at step 2. Training silently blows up to inf/NaN within ~15-25 steps with no exception and no warning. Verified the mechanism by patching :253 to `torch.where(v_g_corrected > 0, v_g_corrected, updates_node * updates_node).clamp(min=eps * eps)` in an overlay copy: the same 20-step run then stays flat at ~1e-2.
evidence: _adadelta.py:252-253 `if noisy_squared_grads is not None: v_g_corrected = torch.clamp(v_g_corrected, min=0.0)` - no where-fallback, no positive floor
_adadelta.py:115-117 `def _rms(tensor_or_zero, eps): return (tensor_or_zero + eps).sqrt()` with adadelta default eps=1e-6 (:321), so a fully clamped v_g gives rms_g = 1e-3
_adadelta.py:267-273 coef = rms_dx_prev / rms_g; dx = coef * updates_node; v_dx_new_t = rho * v_dx_node + (1 - rho) * dx * dx  <- the feedback path
_adam.py:194-197 and _rmsprop.py:126-128 and _ademamix.py:136-140: the sibling branches all use torch.where(v > 0, v, signal^2).clamp(min=bc_floor)

_bias_correction.py:31-34 asserts 'The separate bc_floor clamp seen in some optimizers belongs to the *private second-moment* branch (noisy_squared_grads), where v-hat ... can be genuinely negative' - adadelta has that branch and has neither the clamp nor the fallback
_chain.py:138 and :172-181 auto-route SecondMomentNoiseOutput.noisy_squared_grads into any scaler whose update() accepts the kwarg, adadelta included

tests/test_adadelta.py:296-307 test_negative_squared_stream_bounded asserts `updates[k].abs().max().item() < 10.0` but performs exactly one update from a fresh state (v_dx = 0), so the feedback loop has not started; the same fixture run 8 steps breaches the bound at step 2 (1.51e-1, 7.20e0, 3.44e2, 1.64e4, 7.83e5, 3.74e7, 1.78e9, 8.52e10)
tests/test_adam.py:502-518 is the honest version of the same test (adamw stays at 1.02e-3 for 8 steps)
Realistic-regime repro d=100000, ||g||=1, per-coord noise 1/sqrt(d): frac(noisy g^2 < 0)=0.4999; adadelta step19 max|u| = 9.96e8 vs adamw 4.12e1, rmsprop 7.65e1, ademamix 4.16e1
findings.fix_sketch: Mirror the sibling branches at _adadelta.py:253: `v_g_corrected = torch.where(v_g_corrected > 0, v_g_corrected, updates_node * updates_node).clamp(min=eps * eps)` (this is what OPQ-347's second option, 'actually apply it in the substitution branch', asked for; verified to hold max|update| at ~1e-2 over 20 steps in the realistic regime). Then extend tests/test_adadelta.py:296 from one update to at least 5-8, matching what tests/test_adam.py:502 already implies, so the bound can actually fail. If Adadelta is instead deemed unsupported with private second moments - as Adafactor explicitly is (_adafactor.py:34-38) - raise from the branch rather than diverging, and drop the auto-routing for it.

findings.title: RAdam's private second-moment branch collapses the denominator to bc_floor - the exact failure mode _adam.py documents guarding against - and has no boundedness test
findings.claim: RAdam's `noisy_squared_grads` branch computes `r_t * (m / bc1) / (torch.clamp(v / bc2, min=bc_floor).sqrt() + eps)` (:240). With the default eps=1e-8 (:301), bc_floor = eps*eps = 1e-16 (:348), so every coordinate whose privatised second moment is non-positive gets denominator sqrt(1e-16) + 1e-8 = 2e-8 and an update inflated by ~5e7. This is verbatim the behaviour _adam.py:194-196 calls out and guards against with `torch.where(v_hat > 0, v_hat, m_hat * m_hat)` before the same clamp. RAdam is the only one of the five substitution-capable scalers (adam, rmsprop, ademamix, radam, adadelta) that applies the clamp without the where-fallback, and the only one with no negative-stream regression test at all (grep 'negative' in tests/test_radam.py returns only test_negative_weight_decay).
findings.failure_scenario: radam + mf_gaussian_noise(..., second_moment_strategy=...) via the documented paired-stream flow. RAdam's rectification term r_t is None for the first steps, so the branch looks healthy; once r_t activates the update jumps by ~6 orders of magnitude. Reproduced with the repo's own test fixture from tests/test_adam.py:502 (sq = -ones, both streams at noise_stddev 0.1, lr=1e-3): max|update| is 1.51e-4 for steps 0-4, then 1.95e2, 2.47e2, 2.92e2 from step 5 - it would breach the `< 10.0` bound that the adam/rmsprop/ademamix versions of that test assert, if the test existed for radam. In the realistic d=100000 regime (49.6% of the state nu non-positive) max|update| goes from 1.66e-2 at step 4 to 1.75e4 at step 5 and stays at ~4e4, ~1000x adamw's bounded ~20 on identical inputs. Training does not NaN immediately - it silently takes enormous steps once rectification turns on.
evidence: _radam.py:237-245 the noisy_squared_grads branch: `r_t * (m / bc1) / (torch.clamp(v / bc2, min=bc_floor).sqrt() + eps)` - clamp only, no torch.where fallback
_radam.py:301 eps default 1e-8; :348 `bc_floor = eps * eps` = 1e-16 -> denominator floor 2e-8
_adam.py:194-197 the contrasting guard and its comment: 'instead of collapsing the denominator to bc_floor -> infinity update'
_rmsprop.py:128, _ademamix.py:138 - same where-fallback present
tests/: test_adam.py:502, test_rmsprop.py:239, test_ademamix.py:128 all have test_(second_moment_)negative_squared_stream_bounded; tests/test_radam.py has none
Repro with the test-suite fixture, 8 steps: radam 1.51e-4 x5 then 1.95e2, 2.47e2, 2.92e2 (adamw/rmsprop/ademamix flat at ~1e-3)
Repro at d=100000, ||g||=1, per-coord noise 1/sqrt(d): frac(nu <= 0) = 0.496 every step; max|update| 1.66e-2 (step 4) -> 1.75e4 (step 5) -> 3.95e4 (step 11)
findings.fix_sketch: At _radam.py:240 apply the same guard as _adam.py:197: `v_eff = torch.where(v / bc2 > 0, v / bc2, (m / bc1) * (m / bc1)).clamp(min=bc_floor)` and divide by `v_eff.sqrt() + eps`. Add tests/test_radam.py::test_negative_squared_stream_bounded modelled on tests/test_adam.py:502 but run for enough steps that r_t is not None (>= 6 with the default betas), asserting the same `< 10.0` magnitude bound.

findings.title: Exact-equality drift audit (#872) false-positives on bit-identical optimizer state when ranks differ in intra-op thread count
findings.claim: The #872 fix sets atol=0.0 and rtol=0.0 on _assert_float_equal, so the four tensor fingerprint statistics (:119-122) are compared bit-exactly. Those statistics are computed locally with `t.sum()` / `(t*t).sum()` on each rank (:118-120), and torch's CPU reduction is order-dependent in the number of intra-op threads, so two ranks holding byte-identical state can produce fingerprints differing by 1 ULP and the audit raises. The docstring's mitigation - ':78 Assumes ranks share an intra-op thread count, which standard launchers guarantee' - is an assumption, not a guarantee: it does not cover heterogeneous CPU core counts or per-node OMP_NUM_THREADS, nor differing CPU vector ISAs across nodes, nor mixed accelerator models. Before #872 the rtol=1e-5 default absorbed this class of artifact.
findings.failure_scenario: Two gloo ranks constructed with an identical AdamState (a 5,000,000-element float32 leaf built from the same seed, so bit-equal on both ranks) but torch.set_num_threads(4) on rank 0 and (1) on rank 1. Both ranks raise OperationError: "AdamState.mu['w'].sumsq mismatch across ranks: min=4997394.779571936, max=4997394.7795719365" - a 1-ULP difference produced entirely by the audit's own local reduction. A user who calls sync(opt_state) / sync_optimizer_state defensively on a CPU cluster whose nodes are not thread-count-identical gets a hard training abort on healthy state. The same local nondeterminism is directly observable single-process: the same 5M-element float32 tensor gives sum = -650.3623083472755 at 1/4/8 threads but -650.3623083472758 at 2 threads, and sumsq = 4997394.779571936 at 1/2 threads vs 4997394.7795719365 at 4/8. Blast radius is limited because no production path calls this audit - _dp_trainer.py:2231 syncs only clip_state and aux, never ctx.opt_state.
evidence: distributed.py:80-86 `assert_scalar_equal(float(value), name=name, atol=0.0, rtol=0.0, compute_dtype=torch.float64)`
distributed.py:118-122 the statistics are reduced locally per rank before the collective: `t = tensor.detach().double(); _assert_float_equal(float(t.sum().item()), ...)`
packages/opaque-engine/src/opaque/api/engine/distributed/_state.py:66-72 `torch.isclose(min, max, atol=atol, rtol=rtol)` - with both zero this is exact equality

2-rank gloo repro with bit-identical AdamState and threads {rank0: 4, rank1: 1}: both ranks raise OperationError "AdamState.mu['w'].sumsq mismatch across ranks: min=4997394.779571936, max=4997394.7795719365"
Single-process thread sweep on the same tensor: sum/sumsq differ in the last ULP between 1, 2 and 4 threads
git show 6ea47e6e - the commit that introduced atol=0.0/rtol=0.0; before it the call used assert_scalar_equal's rtol=1e-5 default

packages/opaque-transformers/src/opaque/api/transformers/trainer/_dp_trainer.py:2231 `ctx.clip_state, aux = _opaque_sync(ctx.clip_state, aux)` - opt_state is never synced, so the audit has no production caller
findings.fix_sketch: Either (a) make the fingerprint reduction order-independent before comparing - e.g. reduce with a fixed grain (`t.flatten().view(-1, k).sum(0).sum()` or torch.set_num_threads-invariant kahan accumulation) - or (b) keep float64 but restore a tolerance that is tight relative to the drift being hunted yet above ULP noise, e.g. rtol=1e-12 at tensor scale, which still catches the 1e-6 relative drift the new ddp test pins while absorbing last-bit reduction artifacts. Option (b) is a one-line change and keeps test_optimizer_state_audit_detects_micro_scale_drift passing. Also soften distributed.py:77-78, which currently states the thread-count assumption as a launcher guarantee.

findings.title: The optimizer chain silently discards a privately-released second-moment stream for optimizers that do not consume it, inflating first-moment noise by sqrt((D1+D2)/D1) for nothing
findings.claim: `_route_second_moment_output` (:169-176) inspects the moment scaler's signature (:138) and, when it does not accept `noisy_squared_grads`, does `return _route_noisy_pytree(updates.noisy_grads)` (:172-173, the drop is at :173) - dropping `updates.noisy_squared_grads` with no error, no warning and no record. adafactor, adagrad, sgd and lion all take that path. Meanwhile the paired mechanism that produced the output has already split a joint Mahalanobis budget across the two streams: paired_noise_stddevs (packages/opaque-engine/src/opaque/api/engine/noise_allocation.py:165-174) sets sigma1 = nm*sqrt(D1*(D1+D2)) instead of the single-stream nm*D1, so the first-moment gradient the optimizer does use carries a factor sqrt((D1+D2)/D1) more noise - sqrt(2) ~ 1.41x for equal sensitivities - purchased for a release that is thrown away.
findings.failure_scenario: A user builds mf_gaussian_noise(..., second_moment_strategy=...) as shown in docs/reference/optimizers.md:113-138 and pairs it with adafactor - which the same page (:50) calls the 'Recommended default for DP LM fine-tuning'. Every step, the privatised g-squared release is discarded; the run consumes exactly the same epsilon as a correctly-paired run but trains on ~41% noisier gradients than a single-stream run at the same epsilon would have. Verified: feeding SecondMomentNoiseOutput whose squared stream is a constant -1e9 to adafactor, adagrad, sgd and lion changes nothing in the resulting update and emits zero warnings (adafactor update[0,0] = 8.170018e-04 either way). The reference table at docs/reference/optimizers.md:44-52 lists second-moment support per optimizer, but nothing at runtime tells a user they picked a combination that wastes budget. Privacy accounting stays valid and conservative - this is a utility and budget-hygiene defect, not a privacy loss.
evidence: _chain.py:138 `accepts_second_moment = "noisy_squared_grads" in moment_update_params or any(...VAR_KEYWORD...)`

_chain.py:169-173 `if not isinstance(updates, SecondMomentNoiseOutput): return _route_noisy_pytree(updates)` / `if not accepts_second_moment: return _route_noisy_pytree(updates.noisy_grads)` - the squared stream is simply not referenced
packages/opaque-engine/src/opaque/api/engine/noise_allocation.py:165-174 sigma1_g = nm*sqrt(D1_g*S), S = sum(D1+D2) - the first stream is deliberately over-noised to pay for the second
packages/opaque-dpftrl/src/opaque/api/dpftrl/noise/_second_moment.py:146-151 calls paired_noise_stddevs with both sensitivities whenever second_moment_strategy is set
Repro: adafactor/adagrad/sgd/lion given SecondMomentNoiseOutput with a -1e9 squared stream produce identical updates and no warnings (warnings.catch_warnings(record=True) empty)
_adafactor.py:34-38 documents that the substitution path is not offered for Adafactor, but the chain drops the stream rather than surfacing that at the call site
findings.fix_sketch: At _chain.py:172-173, raise a ConfigurationError naming the optimizer and pointing at the supported set, or at minimum emit a warnings.warn once per optimizer instance: a SecondMomentNoiseOutput reaching a scaler that cannot consume it is always a misconfiguration, since the user paid for the second release. A softer variant is to let mf_gaussian_noise/clipped_grad accept the optimizer (or a capability flag) so the paired budget split is only taken when the consumer exists.

delta_reviewed: Full delta for packages/opaque-optimizers between 4b13d82 and 12146ec4: six commits touching the package (git log --oneline 4b13d82..12146ec4 -- packages/opaque-optimizers), net 17 files / +323 -145. (1) 7b26f655 feat(exceptions) #760 - the bulk of the diff: a mechanical ValueError->ConfigurationError / TypeError->InputTypeError migration across _adadelta, _adafactor, _adagrad, _adam, _ademamix, _bias_correction, _chain, _lion, _radam, _rmsprop, _schedule_free, _sgd. Checked for back-compat breakage: ConfigurationError subclasses ValueError and InputTypeError subclasses TypeError (packages/opaque-base/src/opaque/api/base/exceptions/__init__.py:27,31), so existing except-clauses still catch; no behavioural change, 232 optimizer tests pass. The one place the taxonomy does change a base class is outside this package - tests/test_state_dict.py:532 now expects CheckpointError (an OperationError/RuntimeError) where malformed state dicts previously raised TypeError, raised from packages/opaque-engine/.../serialization/_structural.py:51,69; I left that to the engine reviewer. (2) 51fcf562 #851 (OPQ-347), (3) 8a370bec #861 (OPQ-346), (4) 7bfba532 #863 (OPQ-345), (5) 6ea47e6e #872 (OPQ-344) - the four assigned fixes, verified individually above. (6) ebb2e2c3 #1027 touches only the _schedule_free module docstring (:41-45); I checked the new claim that trainers must 'reconstruct y_t from the saved z_t and x_t when resuming' against update_fn's y_{t+1} = (1-beta) z + beta x at :187-190 and against the trainer's reconstruction at _dp_trainer.py:5567-5570 - the formula matches, and since schedule_free() returns a GradientTransformation whose state IS a ScheduleFreeState (not a chain tuple), the trainer's isinstance dispatch reaches it; the rest of #1027 is transformers code and I left it to that reviewer, flagging only that _restore_params_from_model (_dp_trainer.py:4920-4927) overwrites opt_state.x with the reloaded module params. Beyond the fix commits I also ran the whole package suite (232 passed) and the distributed lane (2 passed), swept every optimizer's private second-moment branch for the OPQ-347 guard pattern (adam/rmsprop/ademamix guarded, adadelta and radam not - two findings), swept the test suite for the OPQ-346 vacuous-assertion pattern (test_adadelta.py:296 is a single-step version of a multi-step invariant; test_radam.py has no such test at all), swept for the OPQ-345 docstring-vs-default pattern across all nine factories (clean), and audited the sibling assert_scalar_equal call sites outside the package (engine gradients.py:74,88,93 still compare public DP metadata - max_norm / noise_stddev - through the float32 rtol=1e-5 default; I judged that below the reporting bar because real config divergence at those magnitudes is still caught, and it is engine-owned). No duplicates of #813/#828/#845 or of anything in other-open-issues.tsv; finding 1 and 2 are adjacent to but distinct from open #407 (JME second moments for DP-SGD), which is about implementing the estimator, not about the consumer branches' negative-value handling.
